chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Yaqub ibn Shu'ayb, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the person in Ihram wearing the buttoned Taylasan, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes,' and in the Book of Ali (peace be upon him): 'A Taylasan is not worn until its buttons are removed.' So my father narrated to me: 'That is disliked out of fear that the ignorant one would place buttons upon it.'

key_terms.الطَّيْلَسَانَ: A type of cloak or mantle worn by Arabs
key_terms.الْجَاهِلُ: The ignorant person (one lacking knowledge of specific rulings)
key_terms.الْمُحْرِمِ: The person in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on wearing a buttoned cloak while in Ihram?
ai.summary: This narration highlights the distinction between the prohibition of buttons on the Taylasan in the Book of Ali and the Imam's explanation that the dislike (karahat) is precautionary to prevent ignorance from leading to invalidation. It underscores the Shia scholarly principle of distinguishing between absolute prohibition and recommended caution in ritual purity and dress during Ihram. The context reflects the practical legal reasoning used to maintain the integrity of the pilgrimage garments against common errors.
